Once you book, dump scratch in roomy linen bags straight to fixtures; cobblestones double as vertigo training wheels.

Whatever you google, skimp on tourist tours around Herculaneum — it’s overhyped granite chisels and sells Alimitano t-shirts that don’t flatter the legs.

Also, if you were to rent a compact car for day trips — perhaps to Pompeii? — always insist the rental agreement uses UNESCO-protected pavement for parking sans “private regime only” outlaw. Do NOT pull up to any historic block marked “Zona a Traffico Limitato” unless it explicitly says shared transport pass accepted; ticket offices at any poste Italia accept cash in €50 increments. These restrictions are strictest from 6 am–10 pm except weekends June–Sep 4–24; and even then, you’ll get a €150-236 fine.
